sections.title: Study area: Mer de Glace
sections.html: Mer de Glace, Chamonix-Mont-Blanc, Haute-Savoie, France (RGI 7 G-11-00757, GLIMS G006934E45883N). The picture box is 13.27 x 15.27 km (set by the owner); the 3D strip along the glacier is 7385 m long and 4826 m wide, 35.6 km² (computed from the saved strip).

sections.title: What was measured
sections.html:
One measured surface, modelled for the other years. The 3D view of Mer de Glace shows an ice surface for every year from 2013 to 2026, but only one elevation model of the whole glacier was measured on a single survey: the IGN LiDAR HD surface model, flown mostly 16 to 22 July 2022 (the tile metadata give 25 June to 22 July 2022; the anchor day of the model is set to 18 July 2022). It is used as delivered (heights IGN69, Lambert 93; a 5 m cell resampled to 10 m, then 25 m nodes). Every other year is modelled, not measured.

How a year is made: the lidar surface is moved to the day of the picture of that year. The pattern of the change in space comes from the Pléiades elevation-change grids of Berthier, Vincent and Six (2023; Zenodo record 8047784, CC BY 4.0; rates in m per year for 19 August 2012 to 15 August 2021 and 15 August 2021 to 8 August 2022, multiplied here by the years between the stereo dates). The change in time follows the cumulative glacier-wide balance with a seasonal shape inside each year (observatory sheet 1980 to 2022, rounded to 2 decimals; WGMS 2023: −2.46, 2024: −1.96, 2025: −2.94, flagged preliminary; the sheet is about twice the geodetic change, so it is used only for the time shape). 2026 uses an estimate (the median of 2016 to 2025). After the lidar the ten-year ratio of 2012 to 2022 is used; this choice was made after the first check against ICESat-2, and is therefore not an independent test of itself.

The front: the dated length changes of the WGMS (series 0, glacier 353; ±5 m for 2011-2022, ±2 m after) are applied as a cut of the ice mask along the strip axis, from the front of the GLIMS outline of 29 August 2015 (University of Zurich). After 7 September 2024 the front is an estimate: the median rate of −24.1 m per year. Elsewhere the ice extent is the 2015 outline. Where the lidar has no height, Copernicus GLO-30 (shifted by its median offset on non-ice ground) fills the gap. The 3D view shows only the years 2013 to 2026, the years with a modelled surface, and the older pictures are on the map: earlier years are not modelled, because going backwards from the lidar is biased (median +3.0 m against the stake heights before 2013).

sections.title: The ice surface of each year (modelled)
sections.html:
Each year is the surface on the day of its picture. The grade says how it was made: A: tied to the 2022 lidar and the 2021-2022 Pléiades change; B: inside the Pléiades window, scaled by the balance (2012-2020), the sigma from stake heights or ICESat-2; C: extrapolated after the lidar with the 2012-2022 pattern and the WGMS balances; D: an estimate, because the 2026 balance and the 2025-2026 front are assumptions. The sigma is the spread (NMAD) of the stake-height differences of that year, or the pooled value where there are no stake data; it is computed here, not stated by a source. The surface of 2012 (the Pléiades stereo date) is in the build but is not shown, because no picture of that year was picked.

sections.title: How far to trust it: checks, limits and caveats
sections.html:
What the checks say (computed here, never fitted). ICESat-2 shots at their own dates: the model minus the shot has a median of +0.41 m and an NMAD of 2.84 m over 7254 shots (a static lidar surface: median +1.31 m, NMAD 5.1 m). Stake heights of the observatory 2013 to 2022: median −0.25 m, NMAD 1.89 m, n 448. Before 2013 the backward extrapolation is biased (median +3.0 m against stakes), which is why those years are not provided.

What the model cannot do. It is a model: the 3D view shows the surface of 2013 to 2026 as made here, and the surface of a year can differ from the real one by metres, more in the years after 2022 (grade C) and in 2026 (grade D). The bed and the ice thickness are a model, not measured: the data-assimilated ice-flow model of Cook et al. (2023, Zenodo 8037002, CC BY 4.0; cluster C3, 100 m cells) gives the bed as its surface minus its ice thickness (where a yearly surface would lie below it, the bed is lowered to it); its greatest thickness inside the 2015 outline is 374 m and the mean 101 m (computed here). No radar survey of the whole glacier was read, so there are no radar pins in the 3D view. The tributary Talèfre lies outside the strip. The experimental tip outlines (GlaViTU) of the session are not used on the site: they lay about 1 km above the real front where the ice is covered with debris.

Cautions of each source

  • IGN LiDAR HD · airborne lidar, mission 21LHD5QK2. Footprint is not proof of points on every part of the ice (snow, voids, glacier lakes): count valid cells on the real raster. A single 2022 epoch, not a series.
  • WGMS FoG 2026-02-10 · glacier 353 (Mer de Glace). Annual rows are glacier-wide values by the investigators, not stake data. Whether the balance series is the GLACIOCLIM series or derived is for the paper to say.
  • GLACIOCLIM site / OZCAR-RI Mer de Glace (full series: ablation stakes, glacier-wide balance, velocity, snout, meteorology). Owner may need to open the portal in a browser or contact the observatory; no account was created and no message sent.
  • Berthier, Vincent, Six 2023 · Mont-Blanc Pléiades elevation-change grids (Zenodo 8047784). Difference grids, not surfaces: they tie the lidar 2022 to 2012 and 2021 but are not yearly DEMs. The paper's Table A2 with all pair dates is NOT READ.
  • Pléiades Glacier Observatory (CNES/LEGOS, THEIA data service). CC BY-NC: the site is non-commercial, so use would be permitted, but keep it local until the owner decides. Access may need an account (not created).
  • Peyaud et al. 2020 · Mer de Glace model, The Cryosphere 14, 3979. The 2018 radar is unpublished: ask the observatory.
  • Farinotti et al. 2019 · consensus ice thickness. Modelled, not measured. Never present as a measurement.
  • Millan et al. 2022 · velocity and thickness of the world's glaciers. Modelled.
  • Historical measurements: seismic soundings, boreholes, ground radar. Negative result: no published thickness raster or point set found in this pass.
  • ICESat-2 · ATL06 v007 shots over the glacier. Over glaciers ATL06 is biased without a reference surface (Enderlin et al. 2022, search summary, paper NOT READ); quality 0 does not exclude crevasses, snow change or slope effects. The IGN lidar 2022 is the natural referee.
  • GEDI L2A. Whole-orbit files read remotely time out. Footprint quality over steep, snowy ice is also unverified. Not used.
  • ASTER · AST14DEM scenes 2016 to 2026, screened against GLO-30. One scene passes a screen designed to be strict; ASTER is a validation or weak context source here, not a yearly anchor. Snow and cloud in the scenes were not screened separately.
  • ITS_LIVE annual velocity mosaics (120 m, RGI11A, V02.1). Annual composites, not the date of the picked image; mixed cells at the glacier edge.
  • GLIMS · ten dated Mer de Glace polygons 1967 to 2015. Outlines differ in what they include (about 21 to 25 km² versus about 29 to 32 km²).
  • Bolibar et al. 2020 · reconstructed glacier-wide balance, French Alps 1967-2015. Reconstruction by a deep-learning model; label as modelled.
  • GLACIOCLIM · Mer de Glace accumulation-zone stake series (mdg_annual_accu_1996 to 2022). The share carries no unit for annual_smb (assumed metres of water equivalent by the programme's habit, NOT stated); do not use before the unit and the altitude datum are confirmed with the observatory. Ablation-zone stakes and the Tacul/Trelaporte/Echelets/Montenvers cross-section series are not in this share.
  • Jourdain et al. 2023 · surface mass balance in accumulation areas (J. Glaciol. 69(277), 1403-1418). Upper basin only (Col du Midi), not the tongue.
  • GLACIOCLIM · Leschaux (Mer de Glace tributary) stake speed series, MDG_Leschaux_speed_2008 to 2022. No unit for annual_speed (m per year by habit, NOT stated). Do not use before the unit and the datum are confirmed with the observatory.
  • GLACIOCLIM · Talefre (Mer de Glace tributary) stake speed series, MDG_Talefre_speed_2008 to 2019. No unit for annual_speed (NOT stated; the observatory page describes balance files only). Do not use before unit and datum are confirmed with the observatory.
  • GLACIOCLIM · Tacul and Langue (tongue) stake speed series, MDG_Tacul_Langue_speed_1996 to 2022. Period lengths vary: a height change over a period is not an annual value. No unit for annual_speed (NOT stated; the observatory page describes balance files only). Confirm with the observatory first.
  • GLACIOCLIM · Mer de Glace front position series (sheet frontsMDG, 1878 to 2022). Cumulative-looking series with no stated zero and no dates within the year. Compare with the WGMS front rows before use; ask the observatory for the reference.
  • GLACIOCLIM · map of the Mer de Glace snout: profiles Mottets, Montenvers, Echelets and yearly fronts 2007 to 2022 (JPEG). A picture, not data: georeferencing the lines would be our own digitising and must be labelled computed. The orthophoto date is not given.
  • GLACIOCLIM · plot "Mer de Glace" front distance 1878 to 2022 with the measurers per period (JPEG). The two front files disagree in their zero, so neither may be mixed with WGMS length changes without asking the observatory which one is the reference. Values read off a figure are not data.
  • GLACIOCLIM · cross-section surface altitudes ProfilU, Trelaporte, Echelets, Montenvers, Mottets, 1962 to 2022 (xls). Yearly surface altitude at one point or mean per cross-section? NOT stated. Do not use as a DEM tie before the observatory says what a value is (centre, mean, which date). Compare with the 2022 IGN lidar.
  • GLACIOCLIM · plot of cross-section altitude against year (Tacul, Trelaporte, Echelets, Montenvers, Mottets), 1890 to 2022 (JPEG). Values read off a figure are not data. Ask the observatory for the pre-1962 values.
  • GLACIOCLIM · overview map of stakes and profiles: Mottets, Montenvers, Echelets, Trelaporte, profil U, Seracs du Geant, Glacier du Geant (JPEG). Stake numbers on the map should match the CSV stake numbers by profile; the match is NOT checked. A picture, not data.
  • GLACIOCLIM · Langue ablation profile, annual stake balance, mdg_langue_annual_smb_abl_1996 to 2022. Unit NOT stated. Point values on the Langue (tongue) ablation profile only, not glacier-wide.
  • GLACIOCLIM · Langue profile, winter stake balance, mdg_langue_winter_smb_abl_1996 to 2022. Unit NOT stated. Point values on the Langue (tongue) ablation profile only, not glacier-wide.
  • GLACIOCLIM · Langue profile, summer stake balance, mdg_langue_summer_smb_abl_1996 to 2022. Unit NOT stated. Point values on the Langue (tongue) ablation profile only, not glacier-wide.
  • GLACIOCLIM · glacier-wide balance, sheet bilanscentresTacul1979_2012, 1980 to 2022 (xls). Glacier not named in the file; confirm with the observatory. The sheet name suggests the balance is derived from centre profiles of the Tacul sector (our reading of the name only). Decimals beyond 2 are not source precision: round to at most 2 when shown.
  • GLACIOCLIM · cumulative mass balance 1905 to 2022: geodetic, glaciological, reconstructed (Vincent et al., 2014) (JPEG). Values read off a figure are not data. The 2012 to 2019 geodetic points and the 1905 start are NOT backed by any file received.

sections.title: The pictures: one for each year
sections.html:
One picture per year, chosen by the owner from the candidates (main orbit 108; season window 07-01 to 10-20, target 09-30). Sentinel-2 pictures are one L1C pass over the whole box, in the site's colours; the older years are Landsat. Years with no usable picture: 2012.

sections.title: Size page: how this glacier is shown
sections.html:
The Size visualizer shows the outline of Mer de Glace in Area view (2D), which you can drag onto a French city.

  • Outline. The GLIMS polygon of 29 August 2015 (University of Zurich). The area shown is the area the database states for it, rounded to two decimals at most.
  • True size. The outline is only moved, never scaled or turned into another shape.
  • Cities. The boundaries of the communes of Paris, Lyon, Marseille, Toulouse, Nice and Grenoble from geo.api.gouv.fr (Etalab, Licence Ouverte): the municipal territory, not the built-up area.
  • Area only. No ice volume is shown on the size page for this glacier: the volume view needs a stated ice volume, and none was read.
